_about: Public changelog for ukelections.co.uk, one entry per merged pull request on main since 2026-08-01. Written by scripts/build-changelog.mjs from GitHub's merge records and the reader copy in changelog-copy.json. date is the UK date of the merge. Dependency updates, CI and internal tooling are left out.

entries.summary: Research: a ward Census correction and a regional level were tested on later contests and not supported; no published forecast changes.
Research: the ward model's inputs rebuilt on corrected polling, with its back-test figures restated; no published forecast changes.
This changelog, and clearer author and publisher details in the pages' structured data.
One page for every council by-election polling day, with results once declared.
Results for five of the six council by-elections of 26 November 2026.
The by-election scoreboard can now score the research model's locked forecasts beside the published ones.
New by-election barometer page, and the accuracy page now shows how often the same party held the seat.
Research: the first by-election forecasts from the research model, locked before the 3 December contests, for scoring only.
Research: checked whether the ward model's misses line up with local data series; no published forecast changes.
Research: national seat totals built from ward forecasts across six elections; no published forecast changes.
Research: local strength inputs were tested in the ward model and not supported; no published forecast changes.
Research: a runner that makes by-election forecasts from the research ward model for scoring; no published forecast changes.
Research: tests of by-election level and of which parties stand in each ward; no published forecast changes.
Research: the ward model tested against the 2018 to 2023 May elections; no published forecast changes.
Research: council control scored on the May 2026 forecasts; no published forecast changes.
Research: a test of when a ward call is safe enough to label as such; the rule did not pass and nothing is labelled.
Research: the ward model tested against the 2021 to 2023 May elections; no published forecast changes.
Research: weighting recent elections more heavily in training was tested and not supported; no published forecast changes.
Research: discounting old previous results by age was tested and not supported; no published forecast changes.
Research: a notional previous result for redrawn wards was tested and not supported; no published forecast changes.
Research: a ward code bridge for 301 wards that could not be scored in May 2026; no published forecast changes.
Research: rolling tests of ways to use by-election results in the ward model; no published forecast changes.
The polling reader now reads the Brexit Party column and rows it had dropped on the 2024 polling page.
The polling reader now covers the 2017 and 2019 polling pages.
First list of the English wards voting in May 2027, with each ward's previous result where one exists.
Homepage now has a postcode box and this week's council by-elections, and the line on our record is corrected.
Council by-election contest files brought up to date with the 27 November nightly run.
Sourced records of which party is defending each seat at by-elections and at councils electing by thirds.
A by-election forecaster scoreboard comparing published forecasts with results.
A pre-registered side-by-side test of a new by-election swing method; no published forecast changes.
By-elections of 19 November: the last four results.
Fixes for readers: closed candidate lists, county divisions and by-election page titles.
Sources for the 26 November by-elections prepared before polling day.
Stopped email links being rewritten on the page, so updated pages can be sent to search engines again.
By-elections of 19 November: five council declarations, four still to come.
Maps drawn for the 23 councils that had none.
Council maps now use real ward and council outlines.
Official spellings for 11 seats whose names had been made from their web address.
Seat maps now use real constituency outlines, with a map on all 650 seat pages.
Ward pages with little to show are kept out of search results, and council pages now carry ward results.
General election forecast now shows win probabilities and seat ranges, states its assumptions and uses verified polls only.
Homepage puts the most important information first; dark mode and search fixed.
Baselines for every English and Welsh council up in 2027, with evidence for the election cycle of the 65 not yet verified.
Clearer council hub, election dates and data downloads.
Lancashire reorganisation timetable updated from the government's letter of 29 October 2026.
By-elections to 12 November: verified results, defending parties, scorecard rounds and the review.
New voter tools: a vote tracker, chances shown as countable dots, ward history, a postcode answer and a ward map.
Charts now have names for screen readers, the forecast page no longer jumps while loading, and the phone header fits on one line.
Look-up pages for the 12 November by-elections.
Published in advance how the May 2027 forecast will be judged, excluding London where the tests failed.
Third and final London test, using polls from before the cut-off; it did not pass.
Second London test protocol; it still did not pass.
Full forecast run on 25 April 2026 inputs, tested on held-back results; it did not pass the London test.
Tooling to rebuild the election history as it stood on any past date, for fair testing.
Tested London-specific adjustments on held-back results; none was good enough to use.
Greater Manchester mayoral back-test now uses the polls available at the time, with new back-tests from borough votes.
Results are now read from council declarations the morning after a by-election.
Better search result snippets, a 2027 page title and a new About page.
By-election counts checked by hand are no longer replaced by feed figures in the nightly update.
By-election contest data brought up to date using council declarations.
Each by-election is now paired with its own page's starting estimate when measuring swing.
By-elections to 29 October: verified results, defending parties, a scorecard round and the review.
Lancashire mayor: status of the 2028 election and five fixes to the model.
List of 2027 council elections: seats up, election cycle, current control and last election, each with its source.
New council by-election review page, with the September and October forecasts scored again.
Local forecast engine: what went wrong in May 2026, a protocol for testing on held-back results, and one candidate improvement.
The May 2026 local forecast is now scored like for like against the results.
A calendar of next elections with verified council dates; pages that are not ready show a notice instead of an error.
Live data synced, the last good version kept if a download fails, and three by-election declarations corrected.
By-elections to 22 October: verified results, the parties defending each seat, and scorecard rounds.
October by-election results, with presentation improvements.
Live data synced, missing results recovered, and the poll reader fixed.
Motherwell, Wishaw and Carluke is now placed in Scotland.
Independent candidates standing as a group are scored by their best candidate in by-election baselines.
Scorecard for council by-elections from 23 September to 1 October.
Each page now shows when it last changed and opens with its own summary; seat swings, which showed the whole projected share, are fixed; new region pages.
Stopped a second copy of the site being served at another address.
Easier to find elections, clearer sources on each page, and simpler routes for voters.
Projections now say when they rest on a starting estimate rather than local results.
Holborn and St Pancras now shows the statutory ballot paper and no longer says nominations are open.
Candidate lists that failed to download are now retried.
Tables now fit phone screens, and email links display correctly.
Fixed the publishing of linked election datasets for download.
Look up your elections by place, with data integrity checks and better routes into the site.
Fixed how Scottish by-election declarations are shown.
By-election contest pages are now rebuilt by the nightly update that checks they are current.
The footer now says what the site is, who publishes it and what holds it to account.
Links to the AI DOGE sister site.
Holborn and St Pancras by-election page, with refreshed polling and by-election results.
Every council's seat total reconciled, a new locator map tile, and the accuracy claim in the menu corrected.
Corrected a count in the forecast probability notes.
Forecast probabilities are now checked across their whole range, not only for the favourite.
The two by-election records on the site now agree, and three errors found in the process are corrected.
By-elections are now graded against the forecast as published, and a gap in the 20 August scorecard is filled.
By-election results for 27 August 2026, each graded against the forecast we published.
A new index of all constituencies, and limits that keep page titles readable in search results.
Source names were being turned into broken links; they are now shown as text. The www address now redirects.
Breadcrumb trails on every page, and structured descriptions of datasets for search engines.
Westminster polling average updated to fieldwork ending 24 August.
Published the council by-election forecast model in full.
Two status labels no longer use party colours, and preview images now work on Instagram.
By-election pages now name the most likely winner by probability rather than by the central estimate.
Per-page preview images, an RSS feed, and clearer labelling of forecasts that are now archived.
New visual design across the site, and a contact page.
Corrected the privacy statement, and fixed forecast text that showed broken dashed strings.
Link to the site's Facebook page.
Fixed maps that drew every area as a solid rectangle.
Every council by-election gets its own page with a measured projection; fixed the ward demographics behind them.
A proper page not found screen.
The homepage vote share strip is now labelled as our projection, not as polling.
Forecast adjustments are now fitted to past results, older results count for less, and the accuracy page tracks forecasts made since.
The high, medium and low confidence label is replaced by a winner probability measured against past results.
Pages no longer point social media previews at images that were never made.
Refitted the party bias correction on uncorrected forecasts, and blocked it from being fitted on already corrected ones.
Ward forecasts now correct each party's measured historical bias, tested on elections the correction was not fitted to.
The record of the May 2026 forecast as published before polling day can be checked again.
Ward pages now lead with the declared 7 May 2026 result.
Fixed a results cache that had frozen the by-election history at 26 April.
Weekly by-election results are now always folded into the history the forecasts use.
Repaired the by-election results feed so weekly results are no longer lost, and backfilled Clacton and four rounds of council by-elections.
All 3,785 seat pages are now listed for search engines, and ward page titles say what the page answers.
Fixed a font that the browser was blocking from loading.
Removed long dashes from generated text so it follows the site's house style everywhere.
Clacton by-election called at the close of poll.
A second, independent forecast method for the Lancashire unitaries built from ward demographics, with its own methodology page.
Corrected a fact about Lancashire's districts, and stopped wide tables spilling off phone screens.
Reworded where Lancashire ward boundaries came from so the description is neutral, and made the county structure consistent across pages.
Lancashire forecast now says plainly where a division shared between two new councils is approximated.
A dedicated page for the Mayor of Lancashire forecast.
Lancashire forecast now shows drift scenarios and calibrates the mayoral second-preference vote; by-election results refresh automatically.
Lancashire reorganisation forecast rebuilt on newer data, with Blackpool's 2023 election as its base and demographic swing borrowed from similar areas.
New polling trends page, and a hypothetical forecast for a Lancashire mayor.
New forecasts for the May 2027 mayoral elections, using the supplementary vote that is being restored for them.
